configuration: Variant m3agent, the M3-Agent long-video QA configuration. memory-7b-sft (imitation learning on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B) builds one entity-centric multimodal memory graph per pre-recorded video, working through 30-second clips with face and voice tools. control-32b-rl (DAPO-trained from control-32b-prompt) then answers M3-Bench and VideoMME-long questions by alternating [Search] and [Answer] over that graph (m3_agent/control.py, at most 5 rounds). Memory is truncated to the clip at the question's timestamp (before_clip).
sources_read: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.09736 (content snapshot; version not displayed). Read through WebFetch, which extracts text with a model. Raw HTML download was not permitted, so the snapshot sha256 was not checked. Parts read: Abstract, §1, §2.1–2.2 (searched for relevant statements), §3.1–3.2, §4.1–4.4 with Algorithm 1, §5.4, §6
mmagent/prompts.py (memorization, plan, action and verify prompts)

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: Memorization processes each 30-second clip. Detected faces and diarized voices are either matched to existing face/voice nodes (embeddings merged) or added as new nodes. The episodic and semantic entries from memory-7b-sft are embedded and stored as text nodes linked to entity nodes. A semantic entry that repeats an existing one strengthens its edge weights; one that contradicts it weakens them, instead of adding a node. So sensed evidence is admitted, integrated and corrected in the graph.
S->M.locator: §4.1 Long-Term Memory; §4.2 Memorization; m3_agent/memorization_memory_graphs.py:33-67,98-100; mmagent/face_processing.py:149-172; mmagent/voice_processing.py:197-218; mmagent/memory_processing_qwen.py:183-254; mmagent/videograph.py:189-297
S->M.quote: "When a memory generated by the memorization process already exists in long-term memory, the corresponding node or edge is reactivated and its weight increased; if it is new, a corresponding node or edge is added to the graph." (§4.1); "M3-Agent processes the incoming video stream in clip-by-clip manner, generating two types of memory" (§4.2)

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: In each round, control-32b-rl outputs either [Search] with a query or [Answer]. A search runs against the stored graph at clip or node level. Face and voice IDs are converted to character IDs using the face–voice equivalences, which are filtered by edge weight. The retrieved entries are appended to the dialogue. Retained memory therefore decides whether the policy commits to an answer and what the answer says.
M->A.locator: §4.3 Control and Algorithm 1; §4.1 (weight-based voting at inference); m3_agent/control.py:100-131; mmagent/retrieve.py:35-48,237-275; mmagent/videograph.py:328-367,417-513
M->A.quote: "appends retrieved results to the context for the next round" … "If the action is [Answer], the system returns the content and the process terminates." (§4.3); control.py:131: data["conversations"].append({"role": "user", "content": search_result})

A->S.label: absent
A->S.rationale: In this configuration, sensing is a separate offline pass that ignores the questions. memorization_memory_graphs.py builds and pickles one graph per pre-recorded video. Its only inputs are the clip, face crops and voice segments, and the memorization prompt contains no question or control state. control.py only loads that pickle and sends text queries to it; it never calls the video, face or voice tools. Control's information needs therefore reach only memory retrieval at answer time, which is M→A. Truncating memory at the question timestamp is part of the evaluation protocol applied to the stored graph. The question-conditioned retrieval plan made from a video clip (retrieve.answer_with_retrieval with prompt_generate_plan) belongs to the GPT-4o/Gemini prompting baseline and is not used by control.py.
A->S.locator: README.md:68-70,154-173; m3_agent/memorization_memory_graphs.py:33-67,108-113; mmagent/memory_processing_qwen.py:36-181; mmagent/prompts.py:308-330; m3_agent/control.py:23,115-127; §3.1 (pre-recorded video; an actor simulates the robot)
A->S.quote: README.md:70: "Generate memory graphs for each video. The results are saved in `data/memory_graphs`."; control.py:117: mem_node = load_video_graph(data["mem_path"])

M->S.label: reported
M->S.rationale: While a new clip is being perceived, its detected faces and voices are compared with the face and voice embeddings already stored in long-term memory (search_img_nodes / search_voice_nodes). The matched node IDs label the face crops and voice segments (<face_i>, <voice_j>) that go to memory-7b-sft together with the clip, and its prompt says to use these IDs as character references. Stored identity information therefore shapes how the current clip is interpreted. This happens inside memorization, not through a request from Action.
M->S.locator: §4.2 Memorization (Consistent Entity Representation; Memory Generation); mmagent/face_processing.py:149-172; mmagent/voice_processing.py:197-218; mmagent/memory_processing_qwen.py:36-142,176-181; mmagent/prompts.py:308-314; m3_agent/memorization_memory_graphs.py:44-64
M->S.quote: "These tools extract the faces and voices of characters appearing in the clip and return their corresponding identities from the long-term memory." … "Having the face and voice identities, M3-Agent continues to generate both episodic and semantic memory." (§4.2)

A->M.label: absent
A->M.rationale: Only memorization writes the graph. In the configured control path, the graph is reloaded from its pickle for every search and never saved; truncation and the equivalence refresh act on a temporary copy. Each question starts a new conversation. Queries, answers and trajectories go only to data/results/<dataset>.jsonl, an evaluation file that nothing reads back. The paper gives memory construction and updating to memorization and describes control as reasoning over stored memory. It reports weight reactivation only for memorization outputs and describes no storing of control actions or their outcomes.
A->M.quote: "and control, which interprets external instructions, reasons over the stored memory, and executes the corresponding tasks" (§1); control.py:117: mem_node = load_video_graph(data["mem_path"])

record.label: not_stated
record.rationale: Search queries and answers live only in the per-question conversation, which is discarded. The only kept copy is the results file that control.py writes for the authors' accuracy evaluation, which is a research log. DAPO rollouts are training data for the developers, not records kept by the service.

outcome.label: not_stated
outcome.rationale: The only evidence about answers is a GPT-4o comparison with human-annotated ground truth. It is used for offline benchmark scoring (eval_answer) and as the reward in DAPO training on in-house data. Both are outside graders run by the developers, and the service itself obtains and keeps no outcome evidence when operating.
outcome.locator: m3_agent/control.py:57-77,201-206; §4.4 Training (reward R_i from the GPT-4o evaluator)

attribution.label: not_stated
attribution.rationale: Correctness is linked to the trajectory that produced it only in developer-run DAPO training (per-trajectory reward, group-normalized advantage) and in offline scoring. Both use an outside grader. During operation the policy only judges whether the retrieved knowledge is enough, and is told to search again after an empty result. That is retrieval at answer time (M→A), not a check of the delivered answer against its outcome.

revision.label: not_stated
revision.rationale: The service never changes its own mechanism. At inference the weights of control-32b-rl (served with vLLM) and memory-7b-sft are fixed, as are the prompts and code. Both models came from developer-run training (SFT on synthetic data; DAPO on in-house data) before evaluation, which is a developer change. Graph updates (new nodes, stronger or weaker edges, face–voice equivalences) are content used by a fixed retrieval and voting mechanism.
revision.locator: §4.4 Training; §5.4 Ablation Study; m3_agent/control.py:32,141; configs/processing_config.json:27; mmagent/memory_processing_qwen.py:183-254
revision.quote: "We perform imitation learning on Qwen2.5-Omni-7b to create memory-7b-sft." (§4.4); "The training data are sourced from our in-house video dataset" (§4.4); "After DAPO training, control-32b-rl achieves improvements of 10.0%, 8.0%, and 9.3% in accuracy over control-32b-prompt" (§5.4)
revision.what: Nothing is revised by the service. Only the developers change parameters: the control policy (DAPO) and the memorization model (SFT), both trained before evaluation.

later_use.label: not_stated
later_use.rationale: Because the service makes no revision, no later run under one is reported. Evaluation runs use the fixed checkpoints trained by the developers.

notes: I judged only variant m3agent: memory-7b-sft builds a graph for each video, then control-32b-rl answers through [Search]/[Answer] rounds over that graph, with memory truncated to before_clip. S→A is not reviewed. Paper text came through WebFetch, which extracts text with a model; raw HTML could not be downloaded, so the sha256 was not checked. Each paper quote used here was reproduced verbatim in at least one extraction and confirmed in a separate exact-match check. I dropped one Introduction clause because the checks disagreed on whether it says 'construct' or 'build'. Code quotes are verbatim from the local checkout. Left out of scope: the GPT-4o/Gemini prompting baseline in mmagent/retrieve.py (answer_with_retrieval with a question-conditioned plan), the training repositories linked in the README (not at the listed commit), and the personal-assistant demo video. The prior queries and results kept inside one question's dialogue are working context, not memory across interactions.
